Rome

Order of the Mysteries
With the First Anaphora,
which is the Anaphora of the blessed apostles
Mar Addai and Mar Mari, teachers of the East,
according to the custom of the Church of the East Syrians
of Malabar.
Rome
[?]

Order of the Mysteries
General Instructions

1. According to the tradition of our rite, worship is directed toward the east (Abdisho: The Pearl, Discourse 5, Chapter 1). For this reason, the church is built from east to west. On the eastern side stands the sanctuary, three steps above the choir area. The rest of the church is the nave, one step lower, where the faithful gather. The right side of the altar faces north, and its left side faces south. A curtain stands between the sanctuary and the choir area. On the eastern side of the sanctuary is set the holy table, that is, the altar of atonement, on which the offering is presented. On its right is placed the Holy Gospel, in its center the victorious cross, and on its left the book of the Order of the Mysteries. Apart from these, nothing else may be placed there unless it is needed for the service of the Mysteries, that is, the Eucharistic celebration. The chalice is prepared in the southern treasury, that is, the one on the left, together with the wiping cloth and water; the paten is prepared in the northern one, that is, the one on the right.

2. An archdeacon and two deacons (ministers) serve with the celebrating priest at the solemn Eucharistic service. The archdeacon is a priest and wears vestments like those of the celebrating priest: namely, an alb, a cincture, a stole, cuffs, and a cope. The deacons wear an alb, a cincture, and a stole. If ordained deacons are not available, they take their places

In the service, subdeacons or readers. If even these are not available, laypeople—that is, persons who have not received ordination—serve at the Eucharist, wearing a tunic and a belt.
3. At the Eucharist, the archdeacon is permitted to prepare the bread and wine in place of the priest and to set them on the altar while saying the prayers appointed for this purpose.
4. During Communion, only ordained deacons are permitted to carry the paten and hold the chalice.
5. After the rite of breaking and signing, the priest does not trace the sign of the cross on the servers’ foreheads while saying, “May Christ accept …,” unless they are ordained deacons.
6. The feasts of our Lord are called “the Lord’s feasts,” that is, the feasts of his work of salvation. We call those of the saints “commemorations,” but they are called feasts when they are celebrated solemnly. The remaining days are ordinary days.
7. The priest makes the sign of the cross on himself in this way: he places the palm of his right hand on his forehead, then on his chest, then on his right shoulder, and then on his left.
8. When the order of service says of the priest, “He kisses the altar,” this is what it means: the priest actually kisses the altar, or touches it with his forehead, or places his hands on the altar and touches his forehead with them.
9. When the peace is given, the recipient holds in his hands the palms of the giver, which are pressed together. The peace may also be given with the giver and recipient facing one another and bowing their heads slightly.
10. When the order of service says, “The priest opens or extends his hands or his arms,” this is what it means: he stretches out his hands (or his arms) and raises them, but not above his head, with his palms open.
11. The chants and melodies are sung by those in the sanctuary—the first choir.

And those on the bema form the second choir, with the whole congregation joining them; otherwise, the congregation is divided into two choirs.
12. The choir helps the people to sing. Know that new hymns or chants may not be used without permission from the church authorities.
13. When the priest says the prayer of inclination, he bows his head slightly, with his palms pressed together, and his voice is quiet but audible to the congregation.
14. The Gospel, the readings, and the Epistle are read on the bema set up in the middle of the nave, or on the raised area in front of the sanctuary. The priest stands there in a place slightly higher than the bema. On the north side (the right), chairs are placed for the priest and the archdeacon; those for the deacons are on the south side (the left).
15. The bread and wine are prepared whenever they are brought to the altar: either while the litany is being said or before the consecration begins.
16. The priest is not required to strike the paten against the chalice when he says, “At your command, our Lord and our God.”
17. The first three prayers of supplication must not be omitted except out of necessity.
18. The asterisk (܀) indicates a ritual instruction or prayers specific to the Eucharist.

Order of the Eucharist

The priest washes his hands and puts on the sacred vestments without saying anything. The vestments are the alb, belt, stole, cuffs, and cope. The deacons and subdeacons put on the alb, belt, and stole; the other ministers put on only the alb and belt.

They all go in procession to the sanctuary, carrying the cross and the Gospel book, with a censer and lights, as is customary. The priest stands in the middle of the sanctuary, facing the holy table. After placing the cross and the Gospel book in their places, the deacons and the others stand behind the priest. They all bow down together.

The priest says aloud: Your command.
They respond: Christ’s command.

Then the priest begins: Glory to God in the highest. Three times.
After each time they respond: Amen.

The priest continues: And on earth peace and good hope for humanity, at all times and forever. Amen.

They respond: Our Father in heaven, may your name be held holy; may your kingdom come. Holy, holy, holy are you, our Father in heaven. Heaven and earth are full of the greatness of your glory. The watchers and human beings cry out to you: Holy, holy, holy are you. Our Father in heaven, may your name be held holy; may your kingdom come; may your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us today the bread we need, and forgive us our debts and our sins, as we too have forgiven

our debtors. And do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours are the kingdom and the power and the glory forever and ever. Amen.

The priest: Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit.
They respond: From eternity and forever. Amen and amen.

They continue: Our Father in heaven, may your name be held holy; may your kingdom come. Holy, holy, holy are you, our Father in heaven. Heaven and earth are full of the greatness of your glory. The watchers and human beings cry out to you: Holy, holy, holy are you.

The deacon: Let us pray. Peace be with us.

The priest says aloud:
Prayer before the Psalmody.

For Sundays and Feasts

Our Lord and our God, strengthen our weakness in your compassion, so that we may minister the holy mysteries that were given for the renewal and salvation of our nature, through the mercy of your beloved Son, the Lord of all, forever.

For Feasts of the Lord

Our Lord and our God, strengthen those who rightly believe in your name and truly profess an undistorted confession of faith, to minister the atoning mysteries that sanctify their souls and bodies in holiness; to serve you as priests in purity, with hearts and minds cleansed of defilement and far from polluting thoughts; and to praise you continually for the salvation you have granted us through the abundant mercy of your grace, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.

For Commemorations and Ordinary Days

May the adorable and glorious name of your glorious Trinity be worshiped, praised, honored, acknowledged, exalted, and blessed in heaven and on earth at all times, Lord of all:

The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, forever.
They respond: Amen.
The priest begins the psalm section for the day.
On ordinary days, however, he says:
Psalm 15. Priest: Lord, who may dwell in your tent, and who may reside on your holy mountain?
Refrain: With pure thoughts, our Lord, set me before your altar.
Lord, who may dwell in your tent, and who may reside on your holy mountain?
Deacon: The one who walks without fault and does what is right, who speaks truth in his heart and is not deceitful with his tongue.
Priest: Who does no evil to his companion and accepts no bribe against his neighbor.
Deacon: In his eyes, one who provokes God is despised, but he honors those who fear the Lord.
Priest: He swears to his companion and does not lie, and he does not lend his money at interest.
Deacon: He takes no bribe against the innocent. Whoever does these things is righteous and will never be shaken.
Priest: Psalm 150. Praise the Lord in his sanctuary; praise him in the firmament of his strength.
Deacon: Praise him for his mighty power; praise him for his abundant greatness.
Priest: Praise him with the sound of the horn; praise him with lyres and harps.
Deacon: Praise him with [?] and [?]; praise him with sweet-sounding strings.
Priest: Praise him with resounding cymbals; praise him with sound and shouting.
Deacon: With every breath let us praise the Lord.
Priest: Psalm 116. Praise the Lord, all you peoples; praise him, all nations.

Deacon: For his grace has prevailed over us; truly, the Lord is forever.
Priest: Glory to the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, from eternity and forever. Amen and amen. With pure thoughts, our Lord, set me before your altar.
Deacon: Lord, who may dwell in your tent, and who may reside on your holy mountain? How beautiful and glorious is your sanctuary, God who sanctifies all.
The deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.
The priest prays:
Prayer before the sanctuary anthem
For Sundays and feasts
Before the glorious throne of your greatness, my Lord, the high and exalted seat of your honor, the awesome judgment seat of the strength of your love, the atoning altar established by your command, and the place where your glory dwells, we, your people and the sheep of your pasture, together with the thousands of cherubim who praise you and the myriads of seraphim and archangels who proclaim your holiness, kneel, worship, give thanks, and offer praise at all times, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.
They respond: Amen.
For feasts of the Lord
Before the awesome judgment seat of your greatness, the exalted throne of your divinity, the splendid seat of your honor, and the glorious chair of your lordship, where the cherubim who serve you continually offer praise and the seraphim who glorify you unceasingly proclaim your holiness, we kneel in fear, worship with trembling, give thanks, and offer praise without ceasing at every [?], Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.

And they respond: Amen.

For commemorations

To the great, awe-inspiring, holy, blessed, blissful, and incomprehensible name of your glorious Trinity, and for your grace toward our race, we owe thanksgiving, worship, and praise at every [?], Lord of all: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.

And they respond: Amen.

They say the anthem of the sanctuary for the day.

The deacon brings forward the censer and the incense, and the priest blesses the incense, saying quietly:

In the name of your glorious Trinity, may this incense that we offer in your honor be blessed, so that it may be pleasing to you and bring forgiveness of the sins of the sheep of your flock: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever. Amen.

The priest takes three grains of frankincense, places them on the coals in the censer, and makes the sign of the cross over them.

The minister brings the cross and gives it to the celebrant. He receives it with a kiss and holds it out to the archdeacon and the other ministers, and also to the faithful, so that they may kiss it as is fitting. At the end, the minister says: Peace be with us.

And the priest says:

The prayer of “To you, Lord”

On Sundays and feasts

When the pleasant fragrance of the sweetness of your love wafts among us, our Lord and our God, and our souls are enlightened by the knowledge of your truth, may we be worthy to receive the revelation of your beloved Son from heaven. There may we give you thanks and praise you without ceasing in your crowned Church, filled with every help and every blessing, for you are the Lord and Creator of all, forever.

And they respond: Amen.

For commemorations and ordinary days

For all your help and your gracious gifts toward us, which cannot be repaid, we will give you thanks and praise you without ceasing in your crowned Church, filled with every help and every blessing, for you are the Lord and Creator of all: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.

And they respond: Amen.

They open the curtain of the sanctuary. The deacon censes the sanctuary, beginning on the south side and proceeding north. Finally, standing at the entrance to the sanctuary, he censes the people. The priest goes with the ministers and the other deacons to the bema, carrying the cross, the Gospel book, the censer, and the lights.

They say:

To you, Lord of all, we give thanks, and you, Jesus Christ, we praise, for you are the one who raises our bodies, and you are the good Savior of our souls.

The others continue. On Sundays and feasts:

It is good to give thanks to the Lord and to sing praise to your name, Most High.

To you, Lord of all, we give thanks, and you, Jesus Christ, we praise, for you are the one who raises our bodies, and you are the good Savior of our souls.

On ordinary days:

I have washed my hands in purity and have gone around your altar, Lord.

To you, Lord of all, we give thanks, and you, Jesus Christ, we praise, for you are the one who raises our bodies, and you are the good Savior of our souls.

Glory. Forever.

To you, Lord of all, we give thanks, and you, Jesus Christ, we praise, for you are the one who raises our bodies, and you are the good Savior of our souls.

The minister: Let us pray. Peace be with us.

The priest says: You, my Lord, are truly the one who raises our bodies to life. You are the good Savior of our souls and the constant guardian of our lives. To you, my Lord, we owe thanksgiving, worship, and praise at all times, Lord of all, forever.
They respond: Amen.
Deacon: Raise your voices, all you people, and praise the living God.
They respond: Holy God, holy Mighty One, holy Immortal One, have mercy on us.
Glory: Holy God, holy Mighty One, holy Immortal One, have mercy on us.
Forever: Holy God, holy Mighty One, holy Immortal One, have mercy on us.
Deacon: Let us pray. Peace be with us.
Priest: Holy, glorious, mighty, and immortal One, who dwells among the holy ones and finds pleasure in them, we implore you: turn toward us, my Lord, show compassion, and have mercy on us, as you always do, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.
They respond: Amen.
The Order of the Readings
The first reader approaches with the book of readings, to the priest’s right. After bowing his head to the priest, he stands facing the people and says: Sit down and be quiet. The book of so-and-so.
He turns toward the priest and says: Bless me, my lord.
The priest blesses him, saying: Blessed is God, the Lord of all, who makes us wise through his holy teaching. May his mercy be poured out upon the reader and the listeners at all times, forever.

The reader reads the reading from the left side of the platform. When he finishes, another reader approaches and says: Be quiet. The prophecy of … or …
He turns toward the priest and says: Bless me, my lord.
The priest blesses him, and he reads the second reading. At the end of the readings, the deacon says: Stand for prayer.
They all stand and sing the opening psalm of the day. The priest begins the first verse of the opening psalm, and they respond with the second verse. In this way they complete the opening psalm, singing in turn from one side and the other.
On feasts of the Lord, they add: Let us honor his birth, or his baptism, or his resurrection, or … with spiritual songs. Hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah.
Priest: Hallelujah (three times).
Deacon: Let us pray. Peace be with us.
The priest prays.
Prayer before the Epistle
For Sundays and Feasts
Enlighten the movements of our thoughts, our Lord and our God, so that we may listen to and understand the delightful proclamation of your life-giving, divine commandments. Grant us, by your grace and mercy, to gather from them the benefit of love, hope, and salvation, which is fitting for soul and body, and to sing to you constant praise without ceasing at all times, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.
They respond: Amen.
For Commemorations and Ordinary Days, and for the Great Fast (Except Sundays)
To you, the wise ruler and wonderful caretaker of his household, and the great, overflowing treasury

All our help and all our blessings are in his mercy. We plead: Turn toward us, my Lord, have pity, and have mercy on us, as you always do, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.
They answer: Amen.
During the Mysteries, two deacons sing the hymn of instruction before the Epistle.
At the end of the hymn of instruction, the deacon carrying the Epistle goes to read. He stands facing the people and says: Paul the apostle’s letter to so-and-so, my brothers. He bows his head toward the priest: Bless me, my Lord. The priest says: May Christ make you wise through his holy teaching and make you a beautiful mirror for all who hear the words of instruction from your mouth, through the grace of his mercy. Amen.
While he reads the Epistle, another deacon holds a lamp in his hand. At the end of the Epistle, they answer: Glory to Christ our Lord.
Then the deacon says: Hallelujah (three times). They sing the chant for the day. At its end, the deacon adds: Hallelujah (three times).
Meanwhile, the priest quietly says this prayer over the incense:
My Lord, may the sweet fragrance that wafted from you when Mary the sinner poured fragrant oil on your head mingle with this incense, which we offer in your honor and for the forgiveness of our offenses and sins, Lord of all, forever.
He also adds this quietly:
To you, the radiance of your Father’s glory and the image of the person of the one who begot you, who were revealed in the body of our humanity and illuminated the darkness of our flock with the light of your gospel, we give thanks and bow in worship

and glorify you at all times, Lord of all, forever. Amen.
Then the priest goes to the Gospel book and takes it up with a kiss, saying:
Glory to the eternal mercy that sent you to us, Christ, the light of the world, [?] the life of all, forever. Amen.
He holds it out to those in the sanctuary so that they may kiss it. While they kiss the Gospel, they sing: Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John, may your prayer be a wall around our souls. Or: Without being ashamed: At the beginning of the books it is written about me. Repeat. The great book of the gospel of Christ the King, our Savior: four marvelous scribes composed their books through the power of the Spirit—Matthew for the believers in Judea, Mark for those in Rome, Luke for the people of Egypt, and John for the Ephesians. And now, in the four corners of the world, people meditate on their books, offering glory to your great power, Lord.
I have desired to do your will, O God: The great book … and the rest.
Glory: The great book … and the rest.
The priest puts the Gospel back in its place. Everyone sits, and two deacons sing the Gospel hymn of instruction, facing the people. At the end of the hymn of instruction, the priest takes up the Gospel again.
He holds the Gospel book in both hands before his eyes and prays quietly: Make us wise through your law, enlighten our thoughts with the knowledge of you, and sanctify our souls through your truth, so that we may obey your words and fulfill your commandments at all times, Lord of all, forever. Amen.
He stands facing the people, and the deacon says: Let us stand attentively and listen to the holy Gospel. Or: Be silent and still. The people stand.
The priest blesses the people with the Gospel and says: Peace be with you.

They respond: And with you and with your spirit.
Priest: The holy Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ, the proclamation of Matthew, or Mark, or Luke, or John.
They respond: Glory to Christ our Lord.
While the priest reads the Gospel, one deacon stands before him, offering incense. Two others carrying lights stand at his right and left. When the Gospel is finished, they respond: Glory to Christ our Lord. The priest kisses the book and puts it in its place.
They roll up the sanctuary curtain.
The deacon begins the litany:
Let us all stand properly, with joy and gladness (on ordinary days: with sorrow and earnestness). Let us pray and say: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
Father of mercies and God of all comfort, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
Our Savior, our guardian, and the provider for all, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
For the peace, harmony, and stability of the whole world and of all the churches, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
For our country, for all countries, and for those who live in them in faith, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
For temperate weather, a plentiful year, and harvests of [?], and for the good order of the whole world, we ask you:

They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
For the health of our holy father, Pope N., head of the whole Church of Christ, and of Mar N., the metropolitan or bishop, and for all those serving under them, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
Merciful God, who governs all things with mercy, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
You who are rich in mercy and abundant in compassion, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
You who are good by nature and the giver of all good things, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
You who are glorified in heaven and worshiped on earth, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
You who alone possess immortality by nature and dwell in glorious light, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
Save us all, Christ our Lord, by your grace. Increase your peace and harmony among us, and have mercy on us.
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
While the litany is being recited, the priest goes with the deacon carrying the censer to the southern treasury and offers incense over the cup, saying:
Make this cup fragrant, our Lord and our God, like the cup of Aaron, the pure priest, within the tent of meeting, O Lord of fragrant roots and pleasant spices, in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, forever. Amen.

Then the priest pours wine into the cup in the form of a cross, from east to west and from north to south, saying: “The precious blood is poured into the cup of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, forever. Amen.”
He mixes a little water into it in the form of a cross, saying:
“One of the soldiers came and struck our Lord in his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out. The one who saw it testified, and his testimony is true. In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, forever. Amen.”
Again he pours wine into the cup and says: “Wine is mixed with water, and water with wine, in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, forever. Amen.”
They go to the northern treasury, and the priest incenses the paten and says:
“Our Lord and our God, make this paten fragrant like the paten of Aaron, the pure priest, within the Tent of Meeting, in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, forever. Amen.”
Then the priest takes the firstborn loaf and places it on the paten, saying:
“This paten is marked with the holy body of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, forever. Amen.”
The deacon says: “With prayer and supplication, we ask for an angel of peace and mercy.”
They respond: “From you, Lord.”
“By night and by day, throughout all the days of our lives, we ask for lasting peace for your Church and lives free from sins.”
They respond: “From you, Lord.”
“We ask for the unity of love, which is the bond of perfection, in the harmony of the Holy Spirit.”
They respond: “From you, Lord.”

“We ask for forgiveness of sins and for those things that help our lives and please your divinity.”
They respond: “From you, Lord.”
“We ask for the Lord’s mercy and compassion continually, at every moment.”
They respond: “From you, Lord.”
“Let us entrust ourselves and one another to the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.”
They respond: “To you, Lord our God.”
At the end of the litany, they open the curtain of the sanctuary. The priest stands on the bema and, with his hands extended, says:
“To you, Lord, mighty God, we make supplication and petition: fulfill your grace toward us and pour out your gifts through our hands. May your mercies and the compassion of your divinity bring pardon for the offenses of your people and forgiveness of the sins of the whole flock of your pasture, which you have chosen for yourself in your grace and mercy, Lord of all, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, forever.”
They respond: “Amen.”
The deacon: “Bless, my lord. Bow your heads for the laying on of hands and receive the blessing.”
They all bow their heads. The priest, bowing, quietly recites this prayer of the laying on of hands:
On Sundays and feasts
“Lord, mighty God”—repeat—“yours is the holy catholic Church, the flock of your pasture, which was purchased through the great suffering of your Christ. Through the grace of the Holy Spirit, who is of the same nature as your glorious divinity, the ranks of ordination to the true priesthood are bestowed. In your compassion, my Lord, you have made our lowly, weak nature worthy to become recognized members in the great body of the holy catholic Church, so that we may provide spiritual help to the souls of believers. You, therefore, my Lord, fulfill your grace toward us.”

And pour out your gifts through our hands. May your mercies and the compassion of your divinity rest upon us and upon this people whom you have chosen for yourself.

On ordinary days and during the Great Fast

Lord God, extend the right hand of your mercy over the apostolic, catholic Church, from one end of the earth to the other. Protect it from all harm, hidden and [?]. In your compassion, make us all worthy to serve before you purely, radiantly, watchfully, and holily.

Raising his head, he says aloud:

And grant us, my Lord, in your compassion, that all of us together, equally, may please your divinity throughout all the days of our lives through good deeds of righteousness, which satisfy and please the glorious will of your mercy. With the help of your grace, may we be worthy to offer you praise, honor, thanksgiving, and worship at all times, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.

They respond: Amen.

The deacons, facing the people, respond one after another:

Whoever has not received baptism must leave.
Whoever has not received the seal of life must leave.
Whoever does not receive it must leave. Leave, you hearers. Watch the doors.

Know, however, that wherever there are no catechumens, it is permissible to proclaim other suitable sentences here, such as:

Let all those who have been baptized and have received the seal of life stand in reverence and honor, so that they may approach the Lord's table with unity of heart.

Order of worship at the sacrament

When the proclamation is finished, the priest takes the cross from the archdeacon's hands and gives it to a deacon. Then he gives the Gospel book to another deacon. These deacons go to the sanctuary and stand facing each other before the table: the one carrying the cross stands on the south side, and the one carrying the Gospel book on the north side.

The priest and the archdeacon stand on the bema, facing the altar. The deacons spread out before the priest a veil on which the image of the cross is depicted. The priest prays:

To you, Lord God ...

And the rest, as above. While the deacons say the sentences:

Whoever has not received ...

And the rest—or something else in their place—the first deacon kisses the Gospel book in his companion's hands, and that companion kisses the cross carried by the first deacon. They place the cross and the Gospel book on the holy table. Then these deacons stand facing the bema.

The priest begins:

May your priests be clothed in righteousness, and your righteous ones in glory.

They respond, singing:

When the priest enters before the holy altar, he stretches out his hands in purity toward heaven and invokes the Spirit. She descends from on high and sanctifies his body—

At this point the priest bows down and kisses the veil three times, then stands and sings:

And blood—of Christ.

He makes the sign of the cross over those on his right.

The deacons say:

Let us enter his dwelling and worship at his footstool.

They respond:

When the priest enters ...

And the rest.

The priest bows down and makes the sign of the cross as above, on the south side of the veil. Then, on the east side, the priest sings:

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

They respond:

When the priest enters ...

And the rest.

The deacons sing:

From everlasting to everlasting, amen and amen.

The priest bows and makes the sign of the cross on the north side. Then he returns to his place.
The deacons say aloud, facing the altar and bowing slightly:
“Forever and ever.” Repeat.
“Our Lord Jesus, let the right hand of your mercy overshadow and rest upon your people and the sheep of your pasture. Lord, your mercy is forever (upon those who worship you); do not abandon the work of your hands into the hands of the evil one.”
They turn their faces toward the priest and say:
“Lord, confirm your promise, as you promised your Twelve.”
The priest says:
“See, I am with you until the end of days.”
The deacons move down a little toward the priest and respond:
“Be with us as you were with your apostles, through the help that comes from your grace.”
The priest says this three times: “See, I am…” and the rest. Each time the deacons respond: “Be with us…” and the rest, drawing a little closer to the priest.
Finally, they all stand around the veil and say:
“And save us from trials, and grant us times filled with peace, so that we may give thanks, worship, and glorify your great and holy name at all times.”
They all bow and kiss the veil. The priest says:
“May God, the Lord of all, be with us all in his grace and mercy forever.”
Finally, they all kiss the priest’s vestment.
They begin singing the hymn of the mysteries appointed for the day.
On ordinary days:
“I waited patiently for the Lord.” Repeat.
“The body of Christ and his precious blood are upon the holy altar. With fear and love, let us all draw near to him, and with the angels let us cry out to him: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God.”
They respond:
“The poor shall eat and be satisfied. The body of Christ…”
The priest washes his hands at the bema, saying:
“May God, the Lord of all, wash away the filth”

of our debts and our sins with the hyssop of his compassion, and may he cleanse the stains of our transgressions in the abundant sea of his mercy. Amen.

The priest goes to the sacristy on the north side. With both hands he takes the paten on which the firstborn loaf rests, raises it to eye level, and goes up to the altar. The deacon goes to the other sacristy, brings the chalice containing wine and water, and gives it to the priest. Holding the chalice in his right hand and the paten in his left, the priest crosses his hands and raises them.

The deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.

The priest says quietly: Let us offer praise to your glorious Trinity at all times, forever.

The deacons answer: Amen.

The priest continues: May Christ, who was sacrificed for our salvation and commanded us to commemorate his suffering, death, burial, and resurrection, accept this sacrifice from our hands in his grace and mercy forever. Amen.

He taps the paten against the chalice three times, saying each time: By your command, our Lord and our God.

He continues: These glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries are placed and arranged upon the holy altar of Christ until his glorious second coming from heaven. To him belong glory, thanksgiving, worship, and honor, now, at all times, and forever and ever.

The deacon: Amen.

The priest arranges the mysteries on the altar table, covers them with the veil, and says in a loud voice: Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit. On the holy altar let there be a commemoration of the Virgin Mary, the Mother of God.

They answer: From eternity and forever. Amen and amen. The apostles of the Son

And friends of the Only Begotten: Pray that there may be peace in creation.
Priest: Let all the people say, Amen and amen. The commemoration of Saint Thomas is upon the holy altar, with the righteous who triumphed and the martyrs who were crowned.
They respond: The mighty Lord is with us. Our King is with us, and our God is with us; the God of Jacob is our helper.
Priest: The small together with the great—look, all the departed have fallen asleep in hope of you, that in your glorious resurrection you will raise them in glory.
They respond: Pour out your hearts before him. With fasting, prayer, and repentance of soul, let us seek the favor of Christ, his Father, and his Spirit.
The priest stands with them all—that is, with those in the sanctuary and those on the bema—at the doorway of the holy place. Bowing, he says quietly: With our hearts sprinkled and cleansed of an evil conscience, may we be worthy to enter the Holy of Holies, to stand before your altar in purity, innocence, and holiness, and to offer you spiritual and rational sacrifices in true faith.
Then he stands upright and says aloud, with his hands outstretched:
We believe in one God, the Father Almighty.
They continue: Maker of all things visible and invisible; and in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, the firstborn of all creation, who was begotten of his Father before all ages and was not made, true God from true God, of the same nature as his Father, through whom the worlds were established and everything was created. For us human beings and for our salvation he came down from heaven, took flesh by the Holy Spirit, and became human. He was conceived and born of the Virgin Mary, suffered and was crucified in the days of Pontius Pilate, died and was buried, and rose on the third day.

As it is written: He ascended into heaven and sat at the right hand of his Father, and he will come again to judge the dead and the living. And in one Holy Spirit, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father (and the Son), the life-giving Spirit. And in one holy, apostolic, catholic Church. We acknowledge one baptism for the forgiveness of sins, and the resurrection of the bodies, and life forever and ever. Amen.

At the end, the priest turns toward the deacon and makes the sign of the cross over him, saying:
May God, the Lord of all, strengthen you to sing his praises.

The deacon says this proclamation:
Let us pray. Peace be with us. Pray for the commemoration of our fathers, the catholicoi and bishops; of all the priests, deacons, celibate men, and virgins; of all our fathers and brothers; of all our sons and daughters; of all faithful kings who love Christ; of all those who have died and departed from this world in the true faith; and of all the prophets, apostles, martyrs, and confessors here and everywhere. May God crown them at the resurrection from the dead, and grant us, together with them, a good hope, a share, life, and an inheritance in the kingdom of heaven. Bless, my lord.
May this offering be accepted with unveiled faces and sanctified by the word of God and by the Holy Spirit, so that it may bring us help, salvation, and life forever and ever in the kingdom of heaven, through the grace of Christ.

At this point the priest approaches the altar and makes three bows, moving forward with each bow. At the beginning of the first bow, he begins to offer this supplication, saying:
I thank you, my Father, Lord of heaven and earth, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, because, although I am sinful and unworthy, you have made me worthy through your grace to offer before you these glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries of the body and blood of your Christ, so that I may minister to your people

and the flock of your pasture pardon for their debts, forgiveness of their sins, salvation for their souls, reconciliation for the whole world, and tranquility and peace for all the churches.

He goes up to the altar, bows down, and kisses the middle of the holy table, then its right corner, and finally its left corner. Turning toward the people, he says:
Bless, my lord. My brothers, pray for me, that this offering may be completed through my hands.

They respond:
May God, the Lord of all, strengthen you to fulfill his will, accept your offering, and be pleased with your sacrifice, on our behalf, on your behalf, and on behalf of the four corners of the world, through the grace of his compassion, forever. Amen.

Then, facing the altar again, he quietly says this supplication:
Yes, our Lord and our God. Repeat.
Do not look upon the multitude of our sins, and do not let your lordship recoil from the weight of our evil deeds. Rather, in your indescribable grace, sanctify this sacrifice and give it the power and ability to pardon our many sins, so that when you, our Lord Jesus Christ, are revealed at the end of time in the humanity you took from us, we may find grace and mercy before you and be deemed worthy to praise you with the spiritual hosts.

The First Eucharistic Prayer,
which is
the Eucharistic Prayer of the blessed apostles
Mar Addai and Mar Mari, who made disciples in the East.

When the proclamation is finished, the priest says this first prayer with bowed head quietly, without stretching out his hands, because he has not yet received confidence.

Prayer with bowed head

We give thanks, our Lord and our God, for the abundant riches of your kindness toward us. Repeat.
Though we are sinners and unworthy, because of your great compassion you have made us worthy to minister the holy mysteries of the body and blood of your Christ. We ask for your help to strengthen our souls, so that with perfect love and true faith we may minister your gift to us.
Repeat: So that with perfect love...

He kisses the altar, then crosses his hands over his chest and says aloud:

Concluding proclamation

And we will offer you praise, honor, thanksgiving, and worship, now and at all times and forever and ever.

They answer: Amen.

The priest raises his open hand upright above the space between his eyes, with its fingers visible above his head and its palm facing west. At “now,” he lowers it to a little below his chest. At the words “and at all times,” he brings it toward his right shoulder, and at the words “and forever,” he brings it toward his left shoulder, letting his hand extend a little beyond the shoulders as it moves from shoulder to shoulder. Then he turns his face westward and says, while making the sign of the cross over the people: Peace be with you.

They respond: “And with you and with your spirit.”
The priest gives the peace to the archdeacon, as is customary, and he gives it to the deacons.
One deacon, facing the people, says: “My brothers, give the peace to one another in the love of Christ.” He gives the peace to those in the sanctuary and in the choir. Another deacon gives the peace to the people, and the people give the peace to one another. The deacon recites the diptychs:
“And on behalf of all the patriarchs, bishops, priests, deacons, and the entire covenant community who have departed from the congregation of the Church; and on behalf of our lives and the peace of the world; and on behalf of the crown of the year, that it may be blessed and fulfilled by your grace; and on behalf of all the children of the Church who are worthy to receive this offering that is before you; and on behalf of all your servants, men and women, who stand before you at this time. On behalf of them all and on behalf of us all, may this offering be accepted forever. Amen.”
Then, turning toward the people, he says: “Let us all give thanks, petition, and plead with the Lord in purity and contrition. Stand properly and look upon what is being done: the awesome mysteries that are being consecrated. The priest (if a bishop or metropolitan is consecrating, he is to say ‘the high priest’) has drawn near to pray, so that through his mediation peace may abound for you. Lower your eyes and stretch your minds toward heaven. Vigilantly and diligently, petition and plead at this time. Let no one presume to speak. Whoever prays, let him pray in his heart. Stand and pray in silence and reverence. Peace be with us.”
During this time, the priest says this prayer quietly:
“Lord, almighty God”—repeat—“support my weakness in your compassion, and with the help of your grace make me worthy to offer before you this living and holy sacrifice, for the benefit of the whole community and for the praise of your glorious Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.”
When the deacon says, “Vigilantly and diligently,” the priest carefully lifts

the veil from the mysteries, while saying: “As you have made me worthy, my Lord, by your grace, of your body and blood, so make me worthy to stand confidently before you on the day of judgment. Amen.”

The deacon brings forward the censer, and the priest blesses the incense as above. The priest censes the altar while standing at its center. Then the priest says:

Canon
“The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God the Father, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with us all, now”—he makes the sign of the cross over the mysteries—“and at all times, and forever and ever.”

They answer: “Amen.”

He continues with his hands raised: “Let your minds be lifted up.”

They answer: “To you, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, glorious King.”

Priest: “The offering is being offered to God, the Lord of all.”

They answer: “It is fitting and right.”

Deacon: “Peace be with us.”

The priest recites quietly and makes supplication:

Supplication
“Lord, Lord, grant us confidence before you, so that we may boldly complete this living and holy service, with our consciences cleansed of all impurity, wickedness, envy, deceit, and bitterness. Sow in us, my Lord, love and harmony toward one another and toward everyone, by your grace and your mercy, forever. Amen.”

He continues with this prayer said while bowing:
“Worthy of praise from every mouth”—repeat—“and thanksgiving from every tongue, and worship and exaltation from every creature, is the worshipful and glorious name of the glorious Trinity, of the Father

and the Son and the Holy Spirit, who created the world by his grace and its inhabitants by his compassion, and showed great kindness to mortals.

“Your majesty, my Lord, is blessed and worshiped by a thousand thousands of heavenly beings and ten thousand times ten thousand holy angels. The hosts of spiritual beings, ministers of fire and spirit, glorify your name. With the holy cherubim and the spiritual seraphim, they offer worship to your lordship.” Repeat: “With the holy cherubim…”

He kisses the altar at its center, raises his hands, and continues aloud: “As they cry out and glorify you without ceasing, calling to one another and saying:”

They answer: “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord, the mighty God. Heaven and earth are full of his praises. Hosanna in the heights! Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who came and who comes in the name of the Lord. Hosanna in the heights!”

Meanwhile, the priest continues quietly, kissing the altar:

Supplication
“Holy are you, God, the only true Father, from whom all fatherhood in heaven and on earth takes its name. Holy are you, eternal Son, through whom everything came into being. Holy are you, self-existent Holy Spirit, through whom everything is sanctified.”

Then:
“Woe to me, woe to me, for I am undone! For I am a man of unclean lips, and I live among a people whose lips are unclean. My eyes have seen the King, the mighty Lord. How awesome is this place! Today I have seen the Lord eye to eye, and this is none other than the house of God.

“Now let your grace be upon us, Lord. Cleanse our impurity and sanctify our lips. Mingle, my Lord, the voices of our lowliness with the hymn of holiness of the seraphim and archangels. Glory to your mercy, for you have joined those made of dust in fellowship with spiritual beings.”

He turns toward the people, stretches out his arms and opens them toward them, and says:
“Bless, my lord. My brothers, pray for me, that this offering may be completed through my hands.”

They respond:
“May Christ hear your prayers. May Christ accept your offering. May Christ make your priesthood radiant in the kingdom of heaven. May he be pleased with this sacrifice that you offer for yourself, for us, and for the whole world in its entirety, which looks for and awaits Christ’s grace and his mercies forever. Amen.”

The priest recites this prayer of bowing quietly:
“Together with these heavenly powers, we give thanks to you, my Lord.”
Repeat.
“And we bless God the Word, the hidden offspring from your bosom. Although he was in your likeness, the radiance from you and the image of your being, he did not consider being your equal an act of robbery. Rather, he emptied himself and took the likeness of a servant. He became a complete human being, with a rational, understanding, and immortal soul, and a mortal human body. He was born of a woman and came under the Law, to redeem those who were under the Law. He left us a memorial of our salvation: this mystery that we offer before you.”

He raises his voice and says:
“My Lord, we commemorate the suffering of your Son, as he taught us. On that night when he was being handed over, Jesus took bread”—the priest takes the paten in both his hands—“in his pure and holy hands, and lifted his eyes to heaven”—he lifts his eyes to heaven—“toward you, his glorious Father, and blessed”—+++ he makes the sign over the paten three times—“and broke it, and gave it to his disciples, and said: ‘This is my body, which is broken for you for the forgiveness of sins. Take and eat of it, all of you.’”

They respond:
“Amen.”

He continues:
“And likewise, over the cup”—he holds the cup in his hands—“he gave thanks and blessed.”

+++ He makes the sign of the cross over the cup three times, gives it to them, and says: “This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. Take and drink from it, all of you.”
They answer: “Amen.”
He says: “Whenever you gather in my name, do this that I have done in remembrance of me.” And he bows down.
He continues: “And as we were commanded, my Lord, we too have gathered, your lowly, weak, and miserable servants. You have shown us great kindness that cannot be repaid, by putting on our humanity to give us life through your divinity. You have exalted our lowliness, raised us from our fall, brought us from death to life, forgiven our offenses, justified our sinfulness, enlightened our understanding, and condemned our enemies, our Lord and our God. You have brought glory to the lowliness of our weak nature through the abundant mercies of your grace.”
Canon
“For all your help and kindness toward us, we offer you praise, honor, thanksgiving, and worship, now and at all times and forever and ever.”
He makes the sign of the cross over the mysteries.
They answer: “Amen.”
The deacon says: “Pray in your minds. Peace be with us.”
He continues with this hymn of praise: “Lift your eyes to the highest heights, and look with the understanding of your hearts. Seek and contemplate what is being performed at this time, when the seraphim stand in fear before the throne of Christ’s glory. All together, with a loud voice, they cry out praise without ceasing and glorify the body that has been set out and the cup that has been mixed, while the people plead and the priest prays, implores, and asks for mercy upon the whole world in its entirety.”

The priest continues with this supplication, saying it with his arms outstretched.
Supplication
“Lord God Almighty, accept this offering on behalf of the high priest and head of the Catholic Church, Mar N., Pope of Rome, and on behalf of our holy father Mar N., the metropolitan (or bishop), who today stand at the head of our people; and on behalf of the whole holy Catholic Church, and on behalf of the priests, leaders, and rulers; and in honor of all the prophets, apostles, martyrs, and confessors; and on behalf of all the upright and righteous fathers who have been pleasing in your sight; and on behalf of all who mourn and are distressed; and on behalf of all who are needy and troubled; and on behalf of all who are sick and afflicted; and on behalf of all the departed who have left and passed away from among us in your name; and on behalf of these people who look for and await your mercies; and on behalf of my weakness, misery, and poverty.
“Yes, our Lord and our God, according to your mercies and the abundance of your kindness, attend to your people and to my misery, and not according to my sins and follies. Rather, may I and these people be made worthy of pardon for offenses and forgiveness of sins through this holy body, which we receive in true faith by the grace that comes from you. Amen. Bless, my Lord.”
He turns toward the people, stretches out his arms and opens them toward the people, and says: “My brothers, pray for me.” Then he turns toward the altar.
The deacon: “May Christ hear your prayers. May Christ accept your offering. May Christ make your priesthood glorious in the kingdom of heaven, and may he be pleased with this sacrifice that you offer on your own behalf, on our behalf, and on behalf of the whole world in its entirety, which looks for and awaits the grace of Christ and his mercies forever. Amen.”
The priest recites this prayer of inclination quietly:
“You, my Lord, in your abundant mercies that cannot be expressed—repeat—make a gracious remembrance.”

and acceptable for the Virgin Mary, the Mother of God, and for all the upright and righteous fathers who have pleased you, in the remembrance of the body and blood of your Christ, which we offer to you on your pure and holy altar, as you have taught us. Establish your peace and concord among us throughout all the days of the world, so that all the inhabitants of the earth may know you, that you alone are God, the true Father, and that you sent our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son and your beloved. He, our Lord and our God, came and taught us through his life-giving gospel all the purity and holiness of the prophets, apostles, martyrs, confessors, teachers, bishops, priests, deacons, and all the children of the holy catholic Church who have been marked—

+ He makes the sign of the cross over the throne from bottom to top and from right to left.

—with the living and life-giving sign of holy baptism.

And we too, my Lord—repeat three times—your lowly, weak, and afflicted servants, who are gathered in your name and stand before you at this time, have received through tradition the pattern that comes from your Son. Rejoicing, praising, commemorating, and celebrating this great, awesome, holy, life-giving, and divine mystery of the suffering, death, burial, and resurrection of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

The priest raises his hands and places his right hand over his left hand in the form of a cross above the mysteries, and says:

May your Holy Spirit come, my Lord.

Deacon: Stand in silence and reverence and pray. Peace be with us.

The priest continues: And may he rest upon this offering of your servants, bless it, and sanctify it, so that it may be for us, my Lord, for the pardon of debts and the forgiveness of sins, for the great hope of resurrection from the dead, and for new life in the kingdom of heaven, with all who have pleased you. And for this whole great and wonderful saving work toward us, we will give you thanks and praise you without ceasing in your Church, redeemed by the precious blood of your Christ, with mouths

Open, and with unveiled faces. And he kisses the altar.

Canon

As we offer praise, honor, thanksgiving, and worship to your living, holy, and life-giving name, now and at all times and forever and ever.

And he makes the sign of the cross over the mysteries. And they respond: Amen.

The priest bows before the altar and says quietly:

Christ, peace of those above and great hope of those below, establish, my Lord, your tranquility and peace in the four corners of the world, and especially in the holy catholic Church. Bring peace between the priesthood and the kingdom. Put an end to wars throughout the earth, and scatter the divided nations that desire war, so that we may live a quiet and peaceful life in all chastity and fear of God. Not to us, Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory.

And he stands upright and says:

Have mercy on me, God, according to your grace, and according to the abundance of your mercies blot out my sins. Wash me thoroughly from my wrongdoing, and cleanse me from my sins. For I know my offenses, and my sins are always before me. Against you alone I have sinned, and I have done evil in your sight, so that you may be justified in your word and prevail in your judgments. For I was conceived in wrongdoing, and in sins my mother conceived me. But you desired truth, and you made known to me the hidden things of your wisdom. Sprinkle me with hyssop, and I will be clean.

Or:

To you I lift up my eyes, you who dwell in heaven. As the eyes of servants look toward their masters, and as the eyes of a maidservant look toward her mistress, so our eyes look toward you, Lord our God, until you have mercy on us. Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us.

And the deacon presents the censer. The priest blesses it, saying: May it please you,

our Lord and our God, our prayer and the fragrance of our censer, like the censer of Aaron, the pure priest, within the tabernacle of the appointed time, Lord of fragrant roots and pleasant spices, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.

Order of the Breaking and the Signing

And the priest holds his hands outstretched over the incense and says:

Our Lord and our God, make the smell of our uncleanness and corruption fragrant with the pleasant fragrance of the sweetness of your love, and wash me with it from the stains of sin. Good Shepherd, who went out to search for us and found us in our lost condition, forgive me my offenses and sins, those I committed knowingly and unknowingly.

When he says, “Those I committed knowingly and unknowingly,” he crosses his hands over his chest.

Then he says toward the deacon:

Our Lord and our God, make fragrant this deacon who stands before your pure and holy altar.

Toward the people:

Our Lord and our God, make fragrant these people who look and wait for mercy from you.

And toward the altar:

Our Lord and our God, make fragrant this altar, which is established in the likeness of our Lord’s tomb, and his throne, and his body and his atoning blood.

And he stretches out his hands and says:

Bless, my Lord. Bless, my Lord. Bless, my Lord. Our Lord and our God, the mercy of your grace brings us near to these glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries, though we are unworthy—truly, though we are unworthy.

And he crosses his hands over his chest, kisses the altar, and bows.

And he stands and takes the firstborn loaf that is on the paten in both his hands. He raises it up, looking at it, and says:

Praise to your holy name, our Lord Jesus Christ, and worship to your lordship.

At all times, forever.

For he is the living and life-giving bread that came down from heaven and gives life to the entire world. Those who eat it do not die; those who receive it are saved and forgiven through it, and live through it forever.

Deacon: “I am the living bread that came down from heaven. I am the bread that came down from on high,” our Savior said mystically to his disciples. “Everyone who approaches in love and receives me lives through me forever and inherits the kingdom.”

During this interval, the priest kisses the principal loaf in the form of a cross, without bringing it to his lips, but symbolically, above and below, to the right and to the left, and says:

“Glory to you, my Lord”—three times—“for your indescribable gift to us, forever.”

Deacon: His ministers who do his will—the cherubim, seraphim, and archangels—stand before the altar in fear and trembling. They gaze at the priest (if the one making the offering is a bishop or metropolitan: “at the high priest”) as he breaks and distributes the body of Christ for the forgiveness of sins.

“Open to me the gates of righteousness.” Merciful one, whose door is open to the repentant, and who calls sinners to approach him, open to us, my Lord, the door of your mercy, so that we may enter through it and sing your praise by night and by day.

The priest says, while holding the principal loaf in his hands:

We approach these holy mysteries, my Lord, with true faith in your name. By your compassion we break, and by your mercy we sign, the body and blood of your beloved, our Lord Jesus Christ, in the name of the Father—he breaks the principal loaf into two halves, from top to bottom—and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, forever.

He places the half that is in his left hand in its place, but not in its original position.

But [?] he positions the broken piece toward the chalice. Then he makes the sign of the cross over the chalice with the broken piece in his right hand, from east to west and from north to south, saying: “The precious blood is signed with the life-giving body of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the name of the Father and the Son”—from east to west—“and the Holy Spirit”—from north to south—“forever.” He dips a third of the half in his hand into the chalice and moistens it with the blood.

Then he signs the body on the paten in the same way, using the body in his hand, and says: “The holy body is signed with the atoning blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, forever.”

He holds both halves in both his hands and joins them together over the chalice, saying:

“These glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries have been set apart, sanctified, perfected, completed, united, and mingled with one another in the worshiped and glorified name of the glorious Trinity: the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. May they be for us, my Lord, for the atonement of our offenses and the forgiveness of our sins, for the great hope of resurrection from the dead, and for new life in the kingdom of heaven—for us and for the holy Church of Christ our Lord, here and everywhere, now and at all times and forever and ever.”

Then he places the halves on the paten, one over the other in the shape of a cross, with the lower broken end facing the chalice and the upper broken end facing the priest. He bows down, rises, and signs himself between his eyes with his right thumb.

During the mystery, the deacons approach the priest. He signs each of them between the eyes and says: “May Christ accept your service. May Christ make your face radiant. May Christ preserve your life. May Christ nurture your youth.”

They respond: “May Christ accept your offering.”

The priest unwraps the veil that is wrapped around the paten and the cup and says:
Glory to you, our Lord Jesus Christ. Though I am unworthy, by your grace you have appointed me a minister and mediator of your glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries. By the grace of your compassion, make me worthy of pardon for my offenses and forgiveness of my sins. Amen.

He bows down, rises, and says in a loud voice:

Canon
May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God the Father, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with us all, now and always and forever and ever.
He makes the sign over himself, raising his hand a little above his head, and the people join in making the sign.
They answer: Amen.

The first deacon turns toward the people and says this proclamation:
Let us all approach with reverence and honor the mysteries of the body and precious blood of our Savior. With a pure heart and true faith, let us remember his suffering and take comfort in his resurrection. For our sake, the Only-Begotten of God took from humanity a mortal body and a rational, intelligent, and immortal soul. Through his life-giving laws and holy commandments, he brought us from error to the knowledge of the truth. After all his work of salvation on our behalf, the firstfruits of our nature was sacrificed on the cross, rose from the dead, and ascended into heaven. He handed over to us his holy mysteries, so that through them we might all remember his grace toward us.
Therefore, with abundant love and a humble will, let us receive the gift of everlasting life. With pure prayer and discerning sorrow, let us partake of the mysteries of the Church in the hope of repentance, turning away from our offenses, grieving over our sins, asking mercy and forgiveness from God, the Lord of all, and forgiving the offenses of our fellow servants.

They answer: Lord, pardon the sins and offenses of your servants.

The deacon: And let us cleanse our consciences of divisions and disputes.

They respond: Lord, forgive the sins and offenses of your servants.
Deacon: With our souls free from malice and hostility.
They respond: Lord, forgive the sins and offenses of your servants.
Deacon: Let us receive the holy sacrament and be sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
They respond: Lord, forgive the sins and offenses of your servants.
Deacon: In harmony and with our minds united, let us receive communion in the mysteries, at peace with one another.
They respond: Lord, forgive the sins and offenses of your servants.
Deacon: May they serve, my Lord, for the resurrection of our bodies and the salvation of our souls.
They respond: And for life forever and ever. Amen.

Meanwhile, the priest says quietly, with his arms outstretched:
Blessed are you, Lord, God of our fathers, and praised is your name forever, because you have not dealt with us according to our sins. Instead, in your abundant mercy, you have delivered us from the dominion of darkness and called us into the kingdom of your beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ. Through him you have undone and abolished the dominion of death and given us everlasting life that does not perish.

And now, Lord, you have made us worthy to stand before your pure and holy altar and offer you this living and holy sacrifice. In your compassion, make us worthy to receive this gift in complete purity and holiness. May it bring us neither judgment nor punishment, but mercy, compassion, forgiveness of sins, resurrection from the dead, and everlasting life. May we all be witnesses who proclaim your glory, pure sanctuaries and holy temples for your dwelling, so that, when we are united with the body and blood of your Christ, we may shine with all your saints at his great and glorious appearing. To you, to him, and to the Holy Spirit be glory, honor, thanksgiving, and worship, now and at all times, forever and ever.

While this is being said, the priest breaks the Body for those who will receive it, if necessary.
When the proclamation is finished, the deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.
The priest says quietly, bowing: In your compassion, my Lord, forgive the sins and offenses of your servants. Sanctify our lips by your grace, so that they may offer fruits of praise to your exalted divinity, together with all your saints in your kingdom.
He stands and says in a loud voice, with his arms outstretched:
And make us worthy, our Lord and our God, to stand continually before you without blemish, with pure hearts and unveiled faces, and with the confidence mercifully granted to us by you, so that we may all together call upon you and say:
They respond: Our Father in heaven, may your name be sanctified. May your kingdom come. May your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us today the bread we need. Forgive us our debts and our sins, as we too have forgiven our debtors. Do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory, forever and ever. Amen.
On feasts of the Lord, however, instead of “And make us worthy,” the priest says:
Let your tranquility dwell among us, my Lord, and your peace in our hearts. May our tongues proclaim your truth, and may your cross guard our souls. As we make our mouths into new harps and speak with fiery lips, make us worthy, my Lord, with the confidence that comes from you, to pray before you this pure and holy prayer, which your life-giving mouth taught your true disciples, the confidants of your mysteries: Whenever you pray, pray in this way, giving thanks and saying.
They respond: Our Father in heaven, and the rest.
The priest says in an audible voice:

Yes, Lord, mighty God, good God and our Father full of mercy, we ask you and implore the compassion of your grace. Do not lead us into temptation, my Lord, but deliver us from the evil one and his forces. For yours is the kingdom and the power and the strength and the might and the authority in heaven and on earth, now and at all times and forever and ever.
They respond: Amen.
When he says “now,” the priest makes the sign of the cross over himself. Then he turns his face toward the people and makes the sign over them, saying: Peace be with you.
They respond: And with you and with your spirit.
The priest bows slightly and turns toward the altar, saying: The holy gift is fitting for the holy, my Lord, in perfection.
They respond: One holy Father. One holy Son. One Holy Spirit. Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, forever and ever. Amen.
On feasts of the Lord, however, they draw the altar curtain and begin at the altar the hymn “You are awesome.” Those in the choir area respond, and when it is finished, they open the curtain.
The first deacon stands on the left side of the sanctuary and says: Praise the living God.
They respond: Praise to him in his church, and may his mercy and compassion be upon us at all times and seasons.
They say the response of the bema.
The priest’s reception of the mysteries
The priest bows down, takes the first portion in his hands, and says quietly: No, Lord; no, Lord. May your Body not bring condemnation upon me, but atonement for debts and forgiveness of sins.
He continues: Sanctify our bodies by your holy Body, and forgive our debts by your precious Blood.

And cleanse our consciences with the hyssop of your compassion, Christ, the hope of our nature, Lord of all forever.

Then: Lord Christ, though I am unworthy, I bear the riches of your mercy. Show in me, though I am unworthy, the greatness of the power of your awesome mystery, which I receive through grace.

The priest receives the mysteries with fear and love.

Then he bows down, takes the cup in his hands, and says: You have mixed your precious blood in the cup at your banquet for the assembled guests you have invited, O heavenly Bridegroom.

He drinks the blood carefully and continues: And from it you have given my sinful self a drink. Glory to you for your love beyond words, forever. Amen.

Order for receiving the mysteries separately

When the deacons approach, the priest gives the body of our Lord to one of them and says: The body of our Lord Jesus Christ, for the deacons of God, for the forgiveness of sins.

He gives the cup, saying: The precious blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, for the deacon of God, for the forgiveness of sins. Or: A spiritual banquet for eternal life.

The deacon approaches the priest and says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.

The priest places the cloth on this deacon’s hands, and then the paten, and says: May the grace of God be with you and with us and with those who receive it in the kingdom of heaven.

Then another deacon approaches and says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.

The priest places the cup in his hands and says: May the grace of the Holy Spirit be with you and with us.

When the response from the bema is finished, the deacon holding the cup says: Bless, my lord.

The priest turns his face toward the people and makes the sign of the cross over them, saying: May the gift of the grace of our life-giver, our Lord Jesus Christ, be fulfilled in mercy with us all.

They respond: Forever and ever. Amen.
They recite the verses of the response for the day. On ordinary days, however, they say: “My brothers, receive the body of the Son,” says the Church, “and drink his cup in faith in the house of the kingdom.”
Then the priest and the deacons go to the entrance of the sanctuary, with the priest holding the paten, or a deacon holding it for him. If they distribute the body and the blood separately, the priest gives the holy body, saying: The body of our Lord Jesus Christ, for the pure believing man (for the pure believing woman), for the forgiveness of sins.
Then the deacon gives the cup, saying: The precious blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, for the pure believing man (for the pure believing woman), for the forgiveness of sins. Or: A spiritual drink for eternal life.
If, however, a priest [?] or a deacon receives the mysteries, he says: The body of our Lord ... Or: His precious blood ... for the chaste priest. Or: For the deacons of God, for the forgiveness of sins. Or, over the cup: A spiritual drink ...
Order for administering the mysteries together, or the body alone
The priest blesses the people, saying: The gift of her grace ... and the rest as above.
They respond: Forever and ever. Amen.
The priest comes to the entrance of the sanctuary with the deacon carrying the cup, and gives communion to the faithful by dipping—that is, with the body dipped in the blood—and says: The body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, for the forgiveness of sins and for eternal life.
Know that whenever communion cannot be distributed to the faithful by dipping, after the rite of breaking and signing, the priest also signs the other pieces that are given to the faithful with the body of our Lord dipped in his blood.

After the people have received communion, the priest returns the paten and the cup to their places. Then he bows down and receives what remains, saying:
May your living body, my Lord, which we have eaten, and your pure blood, which we have drunk, not bring us judgment and punishment, my Lord, nor sickness or disease, but forgiveness of sins, pardon for transgressions, and confidence before you, Christ, the hope of our human nature, Lord of all, forever. Amen.
The priest goes to the sacristy on the right side of the sanctuary, where the cup was prepared. The deacon pours wine and water into the cup, and the priest says:
As we have received your body visibly, may your power dwell in us invisibly. May we go out joyfully to meet you and sing you threefold praise, with the righteous who fulfill your will, Christ, the hope of our human nature, Lord of all, forever. Amen.
The priest drinks from the cup.
While cleaning the vessels, he says: Since we have received your body from the paten and drunk your blood from the cup, make us worthy, Lord, to sing your praise in paradise with the thief, together with the righteous who fulfill your will, Christ, the hope of our human nature, Lord of all, forever. Amen.
During this time, the people recite the hymn.
On feasts of the Lord
Strengthen, our Lord, the hands that reached out and received communion for the forgiveness of sins.
Make them worthy to bear fruit for your divinity every day.
Make the mouths that sang praise within the sanctuary worthy to sing glory.
May the ears that heard the sound of your praises not hear the sound of terror, my Lord.
May the eyes that saw your great mercy see again, my Lord, your blessed hope.

Also guide the tongues that cried out, “Holy,” to speak the truth.
Lead the feet that walked within the churches into the land of light.
Renew the bodies that ate your living body with new life.
Grant every kind of help abundantly to our congregation, which worships your divinity.
May your great love remain with us, and through it may we be strengthened to offer praise.
Open the door to the petition of us all, and let our service also come before you.

On Sundays and at commemorations

Our Lord Jesus, King [?], who through his suffering conquered death the tyrant;
Son of God, who promised us new life in the kingdom on high:
Remove every harm from us, and establish peace and mercy in our land,
So that on the day of your appearing we may live before you and go out to meet you according to your will.
With hosannas let us give thanks to your name for your grace toward our race,
For your mercies toward our humanity have abounded, and your love has shone upon our mortality.
You have covered our sins through your forgiveness. Glory to your name for your gift!
Blessed is your glory from within your dwelling, you who forgive sins because of your mercies.
By your grace make us all worthy to give thanks and worship your divinity,
And to offer praise to your lordship at all times. Amen and amen.

At commemorations of the departed and on ordinary days

May the mysteries we have received in faith be for us, my Lord, for the forgiveness of sins.
You are the likeness of the servant and of the Maker, Christ, King of the ages.
Through your body and blood you have pardoned and forgiven the blemishes and sins of all who have believed in you.

Make us all worthy, at your revelation, to go out boldly to meet you,
And with the ranks of the heavenly beings to offer praise. Amen and amen.

The deacon proclaims: Let all of us, then, who through the gift of the grace of the Holy Spirit have drawn near, been made worthy, and shared in receiving these glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries, all together give thanks and praise to God, who gives them.
They respond: Glory to him for his indescribable gift.
Deacon: Let us pray. Peace be with us.

The priest stands in the middle, before the holy table, and prays aloud.

On Sundays and feasts:

It is fitting, my Lord, on every day—repeat—and right at all times and proper at every hour to give thanks, worship, and praise the awesome name of your majesty. For by your grace and mercies, my Lord, you have made the weak nature of mortal human beings worthy to hallow your name with the spiritual beings, to share in the mysteries of your gift, to delight in the sweetness of your life-giving and divine words, and to raise voices of praise and thanksgiving to your exalted divinity at all times, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.
They respond: Amen. Bless us, my Lord.

The priest continues: May Christ, our God, our Lord, our King, our Savior, and our life-giver, who in his grace has made us worthy to receive his body and his precious blood, which sanctifies all, grant us to please him in our words, deeds, thoughts, and actions. And may this pledge that we have received and continue to receive be for us, my Lord, for the remission of offenses, the forgiveness of sins, the great hope of resurrection from the dead, and new life in the kingdom of heaven, with all who have pleased him, through his grace and mercies, forever. Amen.

And they say: Our Father in heaven… and the rest as at the beginning.

On ordinary days:
My Lord, we are bound to offer praise, honor, thanksgiving, worship, and constant gratitude to your glorious Trinity for the gift of these glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries, which you have given us in your compassion for the forgiveness of our sins, through your grace and mercy, Lord of all: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.

And they respond: Amen. Bless, my lord.

And the priest continues: Blessed is your worshipful glory from your exalted dwelling, Christ, who forgives our debts and sins and takes away our transgressions through his glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries, Christ, the hope of our nature, forever. Amen.

And they say: Our Father in heaven… and the rest as at the beginning.

Conclusion

The priest stands at the entrance to the sanctuary, a little to the right, and blesses the people in a loud voice, saying:

On Sundays, feasts, and commemorations:
May he who blessed us with every spiritual blessing in heaven through Jesus Christ our Lord, who invited us to his kingdom and called us to his glory and to his desirable blessings, which neither pass away nor perish nor come to an end—as he promised in his life-giving Gospel and said to the blessed gathering of his disciples, “Truly, truly, I say to you: Whoever eats my body and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in him. I will raise him up on the last day, and he does not come into judgment, but has passed from death to everlasting life”—may he bless our congregation, protect our order, and adorn our people, who have come and delighted in his glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries. May you be sealed with the living sign of the Lord’s cross and protected from every harm, hidden and visible, now + and at all times and forever and ever.

And he makes the sign of the cross over the people.

And they respond: Amen.

On ordinary days:
May our Lord Jesus Christ, whom we have served, celebrated, and honored in his glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries, make us worthy of the splendid glory of his kingdom, of delight with his holy angels, of confidence before him, and of standing at his right hand in Jerusalem above. May his mercy and compassion be poured out upon us, upon the whole world in its entirety, and upon the Church and her children, now + and at all times and forever and ever.

Another

To him who forgave our offenses through his body and wiped away our sins through his blood, glory in his Church. And upon you, his blessed people and the sheep of his pasture, may he pour out his favors. May he increase his mercies and blessings toward you, and may the right hand of his providence shelter you, now + and always and forever and ever.

Concluding prayer for the departed

Hear, my Lord, the voice of our prayer, and let our supplication come before you. Accept our sacrifices and offerings, and forgive the offenses of our departed, as you accepted the first offering, which Abel offered at the beginning, and that of Noah, blameless and pure, and that of Abraham, who believed in the Lord, and that of Job, who endured afflictions, and that of Elijah, the prophet of truth, and that of the apostles in the upper room, and the coins of that widow.

Likewise, my Lord, in your grace, accept the offering of your servant (or: the offering of your maidservant), and make him worthy (or: make her worthy) of the bridal chamber of your kingdom, with all the righteous who have pleased you.

Accept, our Lord, his sacrifice (or: her sacrifice), and pardon and forgive his offenses (or: her offenses). Wipe away all his transgressions (or: her transgressions), his own (or: her own) and those of all his companions (or: her companions).

Merciful Lord, make him worthy (or: make her worthy), this poor servant of yours (or: this poor maidservant of yours), of that spiritual bridal chamber, with the righteous who stand at your right hand.

Appoint for him (or: for her), from this day onward, both rest and remembrance,

and that lasting delight in the glorious and blessed place. There may he offer (or: may she offer) thanksgiving, glory, honor, and worship to the one nature in three persons, unceasingly and perpetually.

May all who have labored in this service today, small and great, and those who recite in this assembly, be made worthy of forgiveness through grace. Bless, our Lord, this assembly equally with your blessings, and the house and the people, and all of us together, now + and always and forever and ever.

Then the priest comes to the middle, before the altar, bows down, and says:

Remain in peace, altar of atonement. Remain in peace, tomb of our Lord. May the offering that I have received from you be for me the pardon of offenses and the forgiveness of sins. I do not know whether I will come and offer another offering upon you or not.

Finished.
